card: Validates block index records and file metadata during startup to catch database corruption gracefully. Corrupt entries in `blocks/index` can cause crashes, out-of-bounds memory reads, or assertion failures instead of a clean initialization failure. With these checks, corrupted indices are caught early and prompt the user to reindex. It also adds unit test coverage for each corruption scenario.
evidence: Author description: "A last block file number of -1 makes it read before the start of a vector. A very large one makes it allocate and read that many file infos. A block without a parent, or with a parent at the wrong height, hits the assert in CBlockIndex::GetAncestor."
Commit message: "Loading then fails with an error, and the node asks for -reindex. Unit tests cover each case."
problem: Corrupted records in the `blocks/index` database cause undefined behavior or unhandled crashes during startup. Specifically, a last block file number of -1 triggers an out-of-bounds vector read, an abnormally large number causes excessive allocations, and orphaned blocks or invalid parent heights trigger assertion failures in `CBlockIndex::GetAncestor`.

risk.why: Flawed block index validation could falsely flag valid node data as corrupted, causing node startup to fail and forcing users into an unnecessary, lengthy reindex.

scope_notes: The diff was omitted from the prompt, but metadata indicates 87 added lines across two files containing checks and unit tests.
summary: Validates block index records and file metadata during node initialization to catch database corruption early. It checks that the last block file number is non-negative and has corresponding stored file info, and verifies that every non-genesis block has a parent link at the preceding height.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided in prompt, so exact validation implementation and unit test coverage cannot be directly inspected.
